clue.text: Nuns left fringe group from America

parts.note: the title by which nuns are addressed, in the plural
L is the usual abbreviation for left
a fringe is the edge of something

explanation.surface: Some nuns have quit a fringe religious group based in the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: The S that ends the nuns carries over to begin the second word of the band's name, so the word break falls inside a block.
explanation.definitionFit: Sister Sledge were an American family vocal band, best known for the disco hit We Are Family.

clue.text: He had a lifetime of rock and roll!

definitions.text: He had a lifetime of rock and roll!

parts.words: He had a lifetime of rock and roll
parts.note: surface reading: a man who spent his whole life devoted to rock'n'roll music; setter's reading: a figure from Greek myth condemned to roll a rock up a hill for ever

explanation.surface: An ageing rocker looks back on a life spent entirely playing rock and roll.
explanation.walkthrough: The music genre turns literal: a boulder (rock) that he had to roll uphill, only for it to roll back down, eternally.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this king of Corinth was punished in Hades by endlessly pushing a boulder up a slope.

clue.text: Poor Ben Stokes drops a South African

definitions.note: a noun here for an African animal; 'South' may do double duty to make it South African

indicators.note: a poor performance is a messy one, so the cricketer's name is jumbled
to drop something is to let it go, so that letter is removed from the fodder

parts.note: the England cricketer's name, taken as written
one S, the abbreviation for South

explanation.surface: England's cricket captain has a poor day and drops a catch off a South African batsman.
explanation.walkthrough: Ben Stokes is an England cricket captain, which makes 'drops' sound like a dropped catch. Losing one of the two Ss leaves eight letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: The steenbok is a small antelope of southern and eastern Africa, so it is an African animal.

clue.text: Protein-rich food for one struggling with weight?

indicators.note: someone struggling with a load is wrestling it about, so these letters get tossed into a new order

parts.note: e.g. means for example, i.e. for one
the six letters of the word rearranged

explanation.surface: A dieter or weightlifter is advised to eat protein-rich food.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark hints at a gym-goer, but 'for one' is the abbreviation e.g. and 'weight' is the raw material.
explanation.definitionFit: The clear part of an egg is almost pure albumen, a protein, so it is a classic high-protein food.

clue.text: Framework left in 17 not for turning

indicators.note: something for turning is to be turned round, so that word is read from right to left
in places the abbreviation for left inside the rearranged word
the cross-reference answer ends with a word meaning wild or wrong, which signals that its first word is rearranged

parts.note: 17-across is EKES OUT; read as EKES plus 'out', the four letters are rearranged
L is the usual abbreviation for left
the word taken as written, then turned round

explanation.surface: A structure is left inside something that will not be turned; the cross-reference keeps it abstract.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference does two jobs: its first word EKES is the fodder and its second word OUT is the anagram indicator, giving SKEE to hold the L.
explanation.definitionFit: A skeleton is the supporting frame of a body or structure, so it is a framework.

clue.text: Luxury car transporting Yoko under a kilometre for money

indicators.note: in a down clue, being under something means coming after it in the entry

parts.note: K is short for kilometre

indicators.note: a vehicle transporting a passenger carries her inside it

parts.note: RR stands for Rolls-Royce, the luxury car maker
Yoko Ono, the artist married to John Lennon

explanation.surface: A chauffeured Rolls-Royce carries Yoko Ono a short distance, for a fee.
explanation.definitionFit: Kronor are the currency units of Sweden (and formerly Iceland), the plural of krona.

clue.text: Insurer denying cover for expensive wheels daughter fitted

indicators.note: something fitted is installed inside, so the abbreviation is placed within the remaining letters
the cover of a word is its outer front, so refusing it strips the opening letter

parts.note: alloys are pricey alloy wheels on a car
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: An insurance company refuses to cover a driver's costly alloy wheels after their daughter fitted them.
explanation.walkthrough: Lose the A from the wheels, then fit the D before the final S.
explanation.definitionFit: Lloyd's of London is the famous insurance market, so it stands for an insurer.

clue.text: Mac button to switch between apps?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a bar-shaped fastener on a raincoat, a mac being a mackintosh
second meaning: a computing verb for flipping between two states or windows

explanation.walkthrough: Mac looks like an Apple computer, which makes the apps feel connected; it is really a mackintosh, a raincoat.
explanation.definitionFit: A toggle is a peg-shaped coat fastener and also means to alternate between two settings or programs.

clue.text: Last of Malaysian rubber Charlie exported — he won't pay much tax

indicators.note: the last of something is its final element, so only the end letter is kept

parts.note: the final letter of the word

indicators.note: goods exported are sent out of the country, so that letter leaves the word

parts.note: rubber is slang for a condom
Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Reads like a trade report: Malaysia's rubber, shipped abroad by someone called Charlie, a tax-shy trader.
explanation.walkthrough: Malaysia is a big natural rubber exporter, which makes the surface sound commercial. A non-dom is a UK resident claiming domicile abroad, a status that has let the wealthy avoid UK tax on foreign income.
explanation.definitionFit: Non-domiciled UK residents have historically paid little British tax on overseas earnings, hence the description.

clue.text: See 1
Hill runner from Togo bang out of order

indicators.note: letters out of order are no longer in their proper sequence and must be rearranged

parts.note: the West African country, taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An athlete who runs hills comes from Togo and has been ruled out after a bang.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hill runner' suggests a fell runner; it is a sled that runs down hills on runners.
explanation.definitionFit: A toboggan is a sled ridden downhill on snow, and it slides on runners.

clue.text: Switzerland with weak defence? Hardly!

definitions.note: the exclamation says the answer is the opposite of weak

indicators.note: a defence surrounds and protects what it guards, so one word wraps the other

parts.note: puny means weak; it splits to guard the country code
CH is Switzerland's international code, from Confoederatio Helvetica

explanation.surface: A sports pundit asks whether the Swiss team has a weak defence, then answers no.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the whole idea of 'weak? Hardly!', i.e. the reverse of feeble; 'defence' looks like football but means one word guarding the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Punchy means forceful and vigorous, the opposite of weak, which is what 'Hardly!' implies.

clue.text: Author Saul dumping wife; acquiring old road house of ill-repute

indicators.note: acquiring means taking something in, so the short pieces go inside
dumping something means throwing it away, so that letter is removed

parts.note: Saul Bellow, the American novelist
W is the abbreviation for wife
O is the abbreviation for old
RD is the abbreviation for road

explanation.surface: A novelist leaves his wife and moves to a disreputable roadhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Road house' tempts as one compound word, a roadside inn, but the road is a separate abbreviation and the house belongs to the definition. Saul Bellow was a Nobel-winning American novelist.
explanation.definitionFit: A bordello is a brothel, a house whose reputation is bad.

clue.text: Berlin regularly turning over loads…quite a big city!

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: the first, third and fifth letters

indicators.note: turning something over flips it, so in a down entry the word is read upwards

parts.note: loads and lots both mean a great amount

explanation.surface: A busy German capital keeps turning over huge volumes; the exclamation admires its size.
explanation.walkthrough: Bristol is a port city in south-west England, one of the largest in the country.
explanation.definitionFit: Bristol is a large English city, though less than enormous, which justifies 'quite a big'.

clue.text: Bearers every now and again lose their bearings

indicators.note: now and again means at intervals, so only every other letter is kept

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: Porters or pallbearers sometimes get lost on their way.
explanation.definitionFit: To err is to go astray or wander off course, just as people who have lost their bearings do.

clue.text: Universal search programs catching American naval vessels

parts.note: U is the film-rating abbreviation for universal

indicators.note: to catch something is to hold it, so the abbreviation is held inside

parts.note: bots are automated programs, like web crawlers that search the internet
A is the abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: Universal web crawlers net American warships, as if hunting them down online.
explanation.definitionFit: U-boats were German submarines, so they are naval vessels.

clue.text: Film about sport that could use a lift?

definitions.note: a description that stands for the noun

indicators.note: about means around, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: a film is a thin layer or skin, as on custard
RU is Rugby Union

explanation.surface: A movie about a sport where you might need a lift to the venue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Film' looks like a movie; it is a thin layer.
explanation.definitionFit: A ski run is a slope for skiing, and skiers are carried up it by a ski lift.

clue.text: See 15
Carefully gets by Speke — so utterly captivating

indicators.note: to captivate is to hold captive, so the words hold the answer inside them

parts.note: the letters run across the three words, after the S and before the TERLY

explanation.surface: Someone scrapes a living off the explorer Speke, who was utterly charming.
explanation.walkthrough: John Hanning Speke was a Victorian explorer of the Nile's source.
explanation.definitionFit: To eke out a living or supply is to make it last by careful use, i.e. manage frugally.

clue.text: Prime telly featuring pole dancing English student

indicators.note: a programme featuring something includes it within
dancing letters move about and settle in a new arrangement

parts.note: telly is British slang for television, TV
the four letters rearranged
E is the abbreviation for English
L for learner, as on a learner driver's L-plate

explanation.surface: Prime-time TV shows an English student pole dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prime telly' looks like prime-time TV, but 'Prime' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Prime and top-level both mean of the highest rank or quality.

clue.text: Local Iron Age development on lake

indicators.note: development turns material into a new form, so these letters are reshaped

parts.note: the seven letters rearranged
L is the abbreviation for lake; 'on' places it after

explanation.surface: Archaeologists find a nearby Iron Age settlement on the shore of a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Regional and local both describe something belonging to a particular area rather than the whole country.

clue.text: Georgian city chamber in which an American goes?

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase standing for the noun

parts.note: Bath, the English spa city famed for Georgian architecture
a chamber is a room

explanation.surface: A grand chamber in Bath where a visiting American goes.
explanation.walkthrough: Americans say they 'go to the bathroom' for the toilet; 'Georgian' suggests the US state or the country Georgia but means 18th-century English style.
explanation.definitionFit: In American English, bathroom is the polite word for a lavatory, where one 'goes'.

clue.text: Note old archdeacon, leader of Anglican prayers

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for note
O is the abbreviation for old
an archdeacon is styled the Venerable, abbreviated Ven

indicators.note: a leader comes first, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the first letter

explanation.surface: A memo about an elderly archdeacon who leads the Anglican congregation in prayer.
explanation.definitionFit: A novena is a Catholic series of prayers said over nine days.

clue.text: Thrown up, passed out, necking port

indicators.note: up in a down entry means the letters read from bottom to top
necking a drink is swallowing it, so the answer is taken inside the words

parts.note: the run of letters after the P and before UT

explanation.surface: A drinker downs port, vomits and passes out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' sits naturally among the drinking words as the fortified wine, but it is the harbour city.
explanation.definitionFit: Odessa is a major Black Sea port city in Ukraine.

clue.text: Trade union participating in exchange study

indicators.note: someone participating in an activity is inside it, so the abbreviation goes within

parts.note: swop is a variant spelling of swap, to exchange
TU is the abbreviation for trade union

explanation.surface: A trade union joins a study exchange programme.
explanation.walkthrough: To swot up is British slang for revising hard for an exam.
explanation.definitionFit: Swotting up is studying intensively, so it fits study as a verb.

clue.text: Picked stockings — cold November outside

indicators.note: outside means surrounding, so the two letters wrap the garment word

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold
hose is an old word for stockings
November is N in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone picks out warm stockings because November is cold.
explanation.definitionFit: Picked and chosen are both past participles meaning selected.

clue.text: Curtsy old, much-loved King welcomes

indicators.note: to welcome someone is to take them in, so one letter goes inside

parts.note: B.B. King, the beloved blues guitarist
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned curtsy greets a well-loved monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'King' looks like royalty, chiming with the curtsy, but it is the blues star B.B. King.
explanation.definitionFit: A bob is a quick bend of the knees, a brief curtsy.

clue.text: British boy starts to engrave steel swords

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for British
a lad is a boy

indicators.note: the starts of words are their initial letters, so only those are kept

parts.note: the first letter of each word

explanation.surface: A British boy begins etching designs on steel swords.
explanation.definitionFit: Blade is a literary term for a sword, from its cutting part.

clue.text: Spooner's dog unwell, sloping off

indicators.note: Rev. Spooner was famous for swapping the opening sounds of words

parts.note: a dog is a hound and unwell is ill; swap their opening sounds

explanation.surface: A poorly dog slinks away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sloping off' sounds like sneaking away, but read literally it describes a gradient.
explanation.definitionFit: Downhill means sloping downwards, heading off and away down the slope.

clue.text: Santa's known for his timeless cunning

definitions.note: a phrase pointing to the thing Santa is famous for

indicators.note: less means without, so the abbreviation for time is removed

parts.note: sleight means cunning or dexterity, as in sleight of hand

explanation.surface: Father Christmas is famed for his eternal craftiness.
explanation.walkthrough: The T for time comes off the end of the cunning word.
explanation.definitionFit: Santa Claus is famous for his reindeer-drawn sleigh, used to deliver presents.

clue.text: Forget for now temperature in coastal area

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation inside the other word

parts.note: the seaside is the coast
T is the abbreviation for temperature

explanation.surface: Advice to forget the heat for a while when on the coast.
explanation.definitionFit: To set something aside is to put it out of mind temporarily, to forget about it for the moment.

clue.text: Fifty-fifty odds at the start still

parts.note: evens is the betting term for even-money, fifty-fifty odds

indicators.note: at the start means only the initial letter of the word is kept

parts.note: the first letter

explanation.surface: Even at fifty-fifty at the start, the odds remain unchanged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fifty-fifty odds' wants to be one phrase meaning evens, but 'odds' belongs to the second piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Even so and still are both adverbs meaning nevertheless or despite that.

clue.text: Mountaineer of the first order getting leg trapped

indicators.note: something trapped is held inside, so the leg word sits within the other

parts.note: A-list means top-rank, of the first order
pins is informal for legs

explanation.surface: A top-class climber gets a leg stuck in a crevice.
explanation.definitionFit: An alpinist is a climber of high mountains, originally the Alps, i.e. a mountaineer.

clue.text: Backsliding morals having a change of sides in the event

indicators.note: sliding backwards in an across entry means reading the word right to left
changing sides swaps right for left, so one of those letters is exchanged for the other

parts.note: the word read backwards

explanation.surface: A competitor whose morals slip changes sides during the event.
explanation.walkthrough: The R (right) becomes L (left) in the reversed word.
explanation.definitionFit: The slalom is a skiing race through gates, a standard event in winter sports.
